services.name: Amazon EC2
services.desc: Virtual servers (instances) in the cloud with full OS control, multiple instance types, and pricing models.
uses: Host web apps, APIs, or any custom workload needing full server control
Run compute-intensive jobs like video rendering or data processing
services.tip: Know On-Demand vs Reserved vs Spot vs Savings Plans. EC2 is IaaS.

services.name: AWS Lambda
services.desc: Run code without servers. You upload a function and AWS handles execution, scaling, and billing per ms.
uses: Event-driven microservices triggered by S3 uploads or API calls
Real-time data transformation in serverless architectures
services.tip: Serverless = no server management. Max 15 min timeout. Pay per invocation.

services.name: Amazon ECS
services.desc: Managed Docker container orchestration. Runs containers on EC2 or Fargate without managing Kubernetes.
uses: Deploy containerized microservices at scale
Run CI/CD build agents as ephemeral containers

services.name: AWS Fargate
services.desc: Serverless compute for containers — run ECS/EKS tasks without provisioning or managing EC2 instances.
uses: Run containers without managing underlying servers
Auto-scale container workloads with zero infrastructure ops
services.tip: Fargate = serverless containers. ECS/EKS still used but Fargate manages the nodes.

services.name: AWS Elastic Beanstalk
services.desc: PaaS — upload your app code and AWS auto-provisions the infra (EC2, ELB, Auto Scaling, RDS).
uses: Quickly deploy web apps without knowing AWS infrastructure details
Prototype environments for startups and small teams
services.tip: PaaS service. Still uses EC2 under the hood. You keep control of resources.

services.name: Amazon Lightsail
services.desc: Simple VPS with fixed monthly pricing. Includes VM, SSD, data transfer, DNS, and static IP in one bundle.
uses: Simple WordPress or small web app hosting
Affordable dev/test environments with predictable billing

services.name: AWS Batch
services.desc: Fully managed batch processing — queue, schedule, and run hundreds of thousands of jobs at scale.
uses: Overnight financial risk model computations
Large-scale ML training data preprocessing

services.name: Amazon EKS
services.desc: Managed Kubernetes service. AWS handles the control plane so you focus on your containerized workloads.
uses: Run production Kubernetes clusters without managing the control plane
Migrate existing Kubernetes workloads to AWS

services.name: Amazon S3
services.desc: Object storage with 11 nines durability. Stores any type of data — unlimited scale, pay per GB. The backbone of AWS data storage.
uses: Host static websites and store media assets globally
Data lake for analytics workloads like Athena queries
services.tip: Know S3 storage classes: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, Glacier Instant, Glacier Flexible, Deep Archive. Also know versioning, bucket policies.

services.name: Amazon FSx
services.desc: Managed file systems: FSx for Windows File Server (SMB/NTFS) and FSx for Lustre (high-performance HPC).
uses: Lift Windows-based file shares to the cloud without re-architecting
HPC workloads (genomics, simulation) needing ultra-fast parallel storage

services.name: Amazon EFS
services.desc: Serverless, elastic NFS file system that auto-scales. Shared access from multiple Linux EC2 instances simultaneously.
uses: Shared storage for a fleet of web servers serving the same content
Content management systems (WordPress, Drupal) on multiple servers
services.tip: EFS = shared Linux NFS. FSx for Windows = SMB/Windows shares. S3 = object storage.

services.name: AWS Storage Gateway
services.desc: Hybrid cloud storage bridge. Connects on-premises environments to S3 with File, Volume, or Tape gateway modes.
uses: Transparently back up on-prem data to S3 without changing apps
Extend on-prem storage seamlessly to the cloud

services.name: AWS Snow Family
services.desc: Physical devices for large-scale data migration and edge computing: Snowcone (8TB), Snowball Edge (80TB), Snowmobile (100PB).
uses: Migrate 80+ TB data center to S3 when internet is too slow/costly
Edge computing in oil rigs, ships, or remote locations without internet
services.tip: Rule of thumb: if data transfer would take >1 week over internet → use Snowball.

services.name: AWS DataSync
services.desc: Online data transfer service to automate moving large datasets between on-premises storage and AWS S3/EFS/FSx.
uses: Weekly scheduled replication of on-prem NAS to EFS
One-time migration of file server content to FSx for Windows

services.name: Amazon RDS
services.desc: Managed relational DB service. Supports MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB, Oracle, SQL Server. Handles patching, backups, and failover.
uses: E-commerce product catalog and order management systems
Enterprise apps needing ACID-compliant SQL databases
services.tip: RDS = managed but not serverless. Multi-AZ = high availability. Read Replicas = performance.

services.name: Amazon Aurora
services.desc: MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible DB built for the cloud. 5× faster than MySQL, 3× faster than PostgreSQL. Auto-scales storage to 128TB.
uses: High-throughput SaaS apps needing MySQL/PostgreSQL compatibility
Replacing costly Oracle licenses with a cloud-native alternative
services.tip: Aurora Serverless v2 auto-scales capacity to zero. Great exam topic for cost optimization.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.desc: Fully managed NoSQL key-value and document database. Single-digit millisecond latency at any scale, serverless.
uses: Gaming leaderboards and session management needing millisecond reads
Shopping cart data that needs horizontal scaling with traffic spikes
services.tip: NoSQL = DynamoDB. Key exam topic: on-demand vs provisioned capacity, DAX for caching.

services.name: Amazon ElastiCache
services.desc: Managed in-memory caching service with Redis or Memcached. Reduces DB load for read-heavy workloads.
uses: Cache database query results to serve millions of API requests
Session storage for web apps needing sub-millisecond access
services.tip: Caching layer to improve performance. Redis = more features. Memcached = simpler.

services.name: AWS MemoryDB for Redis
services.desc: Redis-compatible, fully managed, durable in-memory database. Unlike ElastiCache, it's a primary database — data persists across restarts.
uses: Primary ultra-fast database for leaderboards and real-time analytics
Microservices requiring a persistent, low-latency data store

services.name: Amazon Redshift
services.desc: Fully managed petabyte-scale data warehouse. Columnar storage, MPP architecture for fast analytical queries on large datasets.
uses: BI and ad-hoc SQL queries on years of historical sales data
Complex analytical queries joining TB of data for executive dashboards
services.tip: OLAP = Redshift (analytics). OLTP = RDS (transactional). Know this distinction for exam.

services.name: Amazon DocumentDB
services.desc: MongoDB-compatible managed document database. Stores, queries, and indexes JSON data — fully managed by AWS.
uses: Content management systems with complex nested data structures
User profiles and product catalogs with variable schemas

services.name: Amazon Neptune
services.desc: Fully managed graph database for highly connected datasets. Supports Gremlin and SPARQL.
uses: Social network graphs (friend-of-friend queries)
Fraud detection by analyzing relationship patterns

services.name: Amazon VPC
services.desc: Logically isolated virtual network in AWS. You control IP ranges, subnets, route tables, internet gateways, and security.
uses: Isolate sensitive workloads in private subnets without internet access
Connect on-prem to AWS using VPN or Direct Connect through VPC
services.tip: Key concepts: Public vs Private subnets, Security Groups (stateful), NACLs (stateless), NAT Gateway.

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.desc: Global CDN with 400+ edge locations. Caches content close to users, reducing latency and origin server load. Integrates with WAF and Shield.
uses: Serve static website assets globally with low latency
Stream video content to global audiences with minimal buffering
services.tip: CDN = CloudFront. Know: origins (S3, EC2, ALB), OAI for private S3, Lambda@Edge.

services.name: Amazon Route 53
services.desc: Scalable DNS, domain registration, and health checking. Supports multiple routing policies including latency-based, geolocation, and failover.
uses: DNS with health check-based failover to a backup region
Latency-based routing directing users to the closest AWS region
services.tip: Route 53 = DNS + health checks. Routing policies: Simple, Weighted, Latency, Failover, Geolocation.

services.name: AWS Direct Connect
services.desc: Dedicated private physical network connection from your data center to AWS — bypasses public internet for consistent, low-latency throughput.
uses: Consistent sub-10ms latency for hybrid apps that need both cloud and on-prem
Transferring petabytes of data with reduced bandwidth costs vs internet
services.tip: Direct Connect = private dedicated line. VPN = encrypted over internet. Direct Connect is faster/more consistent.

services.name: AWS Transit Gateway
services.desc: Network transit hub to connect thousands of VPCs and on-premises networks through a central gateway — replaces complex VPC peering.
uses: Hub-and-spoke model connecting 100+ VPCs in a large enterprise
Simplifying mesh VPC peering topology to a star topology

services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
services.desc: Uses AWS backbone to route traffic to optimal endpoints globally. Provides static anycast IPs for global applications.
uses: Improve availability and performance for global gaming or fintech apps
Static IP addresses for multi-region applications behind load balancers
services.tip: CloudFront = cache content at edge. Global Accelerator = route TCP/UDP traffic via AWS backbone.

services.name: AWS WaveLength
services.desc: Deploy AWS compute and storage at 5G network edges inside telecom carrier data centers for ultra-low (<5ms) latency.
uses: AR/VR and live streaming apps on 5G networks requiring ultra-low latency
Connected vehicle and IoT applications on 5G networks

services.name: AWS PrivateLink
services.desc: Establish private connectivity from VPCs or on-premises to AWS services and third-party SaaS without traffic traversing the internet.
uses: Securely access SaaS products without public internet exposure
Private inter-VPC service communication without VPC peering or IGW

services.name: Elastic Load Balancing
services.desc: Auto-distributes incoming traffic across multiple EC2, ECS, Lambda targets. Types: ALB (HTTP), NLB (TCP/UDP), GLB (appliances).
uses: Distribute web traffic across EC2 instances in multiple AZs
Health check-based routing to automatically bypass unhealthy instances
services.tip: ALB = Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS). NLB = Layer 4 (TCP/UDP, static IP). Know with Auto Scaling.

services.name: AWS IAM
services.desc: Control who can do what in your AWS account. Create users, groups, roles, and policies. Foundation of AWS security.
uses: Grant developers least-privilege access to only the services they need
Assign IAM roles to EC2 instances to access S3 without storing credentials
services.tip: IAM is global. Key concepts: Users, Groups, Roles, Policies (JSON), Least Privilege. MFA for root account!

services.name: Amazon Cognito
services.desc: Managed user identity for web and mobile apps. User Pools = authentication; Identity Pools = AWS credentials for authenticated users.
uses: Social login (Google/Facebook/Apple) for a mobile app
Granting authenticated app users temporary AWS credentials
services.tip: Note: Often written 'Incognito' by mistake. It's Amazon Cognito. User Pools vs Identity Pools distinction is exam-tested.

services.name: AWS Key Management Service
services.desc: Create, manage, and use encryption keys across 100+ AWS services. Supports symmetric and asymmetric keys with automatic rotation.
uses: Encrypt S3 buckets, RDS databases, and EBS volumes with managed keys
Customer-managed key rotation for PCI-DSS and HIPAA compliance
services.tip: KMS = manage encryption keys. CloudHSM = dedicated hardware. SSE-S3 vs SSE-KMS vs SSE-C for S3 encryption.

services.name: AWS CloudHSM
services.desc: Dedicated hardware security module in the AWS cloud. You control the keys — AWS has no access. Single-tenant.
uses: PCI-DSS compliance requiring key storage in validated HSM hardware
Offloading SSL/TLS processing from web servers to HSM
services.tip: HSM = single-tenant dedicated hardware. KMS = multi-tenant managed service. CloudHSM gives YOU full key control.

services.name: Amazon Macie
services.desc: ML-powered service that discovers, classifies and protects sensitive data (PII, PHI, financial data) in S3 automatically.
uses: Automatically detect credit card numbers and SSNs in S3 buckets
GDPR/HIPAA compliance auditing — find where sensitive data lives

services.name: Amazon GuardDuty
services.desc: Intelligent threat detection using ML, analyzing CloudTrail logs, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs to find malicious activity.
uses: Detect compromised EC2 instances mining cryptocurrency
Flag unusual API calls from known malicious IP addresses
services.tip: GuardDuty = threat detection (what is happening?). Inspector = vulnerability scanning (what could happen?). Macie = data protection (where is sensitive data?).

services.name: Amazon Inspector
services.desc: Automated vulnerability assessment for EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and ECR container images — continuously scanning for CVEs.
uses: Continuous scanning of EC2 fleet for known OS and software vulnerabilities
Scan Docker images in ECR before deployment to production

services.name: AWS Artifact
services.desc: Self-service compliance portal. Download AWS security and compliance reports (SOC, PCI, ISO) and manage legal agreements.
uses: Download SOC 2 Type II reports for your company's auditors
Review and sign AWS Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for HIPAA
services.tip: Artifact = compliance DOCUMENTS. Config = compliance RULES. Don't confuse them.

services.name: AWS Shield
services.desc: Managed DDoS protection. Standard is free and automatic for all AWS customers protecting Layer 3/4 attacks.
uses: Automatic DDoS protection for all EC2, ELB, CloudFront, Route 53 resources
Always-on protection against SYN floods and UDP reflection attacks
services.tip: Shield Standard = free, automatic. Shield Advanced = paid, includes WAF, DRT team, cost protection.

services.name: AWS Shield Advanced
services.desc: Enhanced DDoS protection: Layer 7 mitigation, 24/7 access to the DDoS Response Team (DRT), cost protection, and advanced metrics.
uses: High-traffic e-commerce sites needing Layer 7 DDoS protection
Financial services requiring guaranteed uptime with DRT escalation path

services.name: AWS WAF
services.desc: Web Application Firewall to filter HTTP/S requests. Block SQL injection, XSS, bad bots, and malicious IPs using rules.
uses: Block OWASP Top 10 attacks on ALB or API Gateway
Rate limiting to prevent scrapers from abusing your public API
services.tip: WAF works with CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, AppSync. Managed rule groups available.

services.name: AWS Secrets Manager
services.desc: Securely store, rotate, and retrieve secrets (DB passwords, API keys, tokens). Auto-rotation built in for RDS/Redshift credentials.
uses: Automatically rotate RDS database credentials on a schedule
Distribute API keys to Lambda functions without hardcoding credentials
services.tip: Secrets Manager = rotation + storage. Parameter Store (SSM) = config + simpler secrets (cheaper).

services.name: AWS Security Hub
services.desc: Centralized security posture management. Aggregates findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, Macie, and third-party tools in one dashboard.
uses: Unified security dashboard across multiple AWS accounts and services
Automated compliance checks against CIS, PCI-DSS, and AWS Foundational Security standards

services.name: AWS Certificate Manager
services.desc: Provision, manage, and auto-renew SSL/TLS certificates for free when used with ACM-integrated services (CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway).
uses: Free SSL certificates for a website served via ALB or CloudFront
Automated renewal — no more expired certificate incidents

services.name: AWS CloudWatch
services.desc: Monitoring, logging, and observability for AWS resources. Collect metrics, create alarms, visualize dashboards, and store logs.
uses: Alert when EC2 CPU > 80% and trigger Auto Scaling
Aggregate application logs from multiple services into a single log group
services.tip: CloudWatch = monitoring & logs. CloudTrail = API audit logs. Know: Metrics, Alarms, Logs, Events, Dashboards.

services.name: AWS CloudTrail
services.desc: Records every API call made in your AWS account — who did what, when, and from where. Stored in S3. Enabled by default.
uses: Audit who deleted a production S3 bucket at 2am
Security forensics for unauthorized IAM policy changes
services.tip: CloudTrail = WHO did WHAT. CloudWatch = HOW IS IT performing. CloudTrail logs go to S3 or CloudWatch Logs.

services.name: AWS Config
services.desc: Continuously records AWS resource configurations and evaluates them against compliance rules. Shows configuration history and drift.
uses: Detect when any S3 bucket is made publicly accessible
Audit compliance: ensure all EBS volumes are encrypted
services.tip: Config = resource configuration compliance over time. Artifact = compliance reports from AWS. Don't confuse.

services.name: AWS Trusted Advisor
services.desc: Real-time best practice recommendations across 5 pillars: Cost Optimization, Security, Fault Tolerance, Performance, Service Limits.
uses: Identify idle EC2 instances and unused EBS volumes to cut costs
Flag security groups with unrestricted inbound port 22 (SSH) access
services.tip: Free checks: Service Limits + some Security. Business/Enterprise Support = all checks. Exam loves this service.

services.name: AWS Health Dashboard
services.desc: Personalized view of AWS service health events that affect YOUR specific resources — not just general service status.
uses: Get proactive alerts about EC2 instance retirement in your account
Check if a regional outage is affecting your specific RDS instances
services.tip: AWS Health Dashboard (personal) = your resources. service.aws.amazon.com = all AWS services status.

services.name: AWS Systems Manager
services.desc: Unified operations hub for managing AWS and on-prem infrastructure. Run Command, Patch Manager, Session Manager, Parameter Store, and more.
uses: Run commands across 1000 EC2 instances at once — no SSH needed
Centralized patch management with maintenance windows and compliance reporting
services.tip: Session Manager = SSH/RDP without opening ports. Parameter Store = config/secrets storage (cheaper than Secrets Manager).

services.name: AWS Organizations
services.desc: Centrally manage multiple AWS accounts. Consolidated billing, Service Control Policies (SCPs), and Organizational Units (OUs).
uses: Single consolidated invoice for all 50 AWS accounts in a company
Prevent all accounts in an OU from disabling CloudTrail using an SCP
services.tip: SCP = guardrails that override even admin IAM permissions. Consolidated billing = volume discounts.

services.name: AWS Control Tower
services.desc: Automates setup of a secure, compliant, multi-account AWS environment (landing zone) with pre-configured guardrails.
uses: Set up a new AWS landing zone with security baseline in hours not months
Enforce guardrails like 'disallow root user access keys' across all accounts

services.name: AWS CloudFormation
services.desc: Infrastructure as Code (IaC). Define AWS resources in JSON/YAML templates and provision them reproducibly as stacks.
uses: Deploy identical dev, staging, and prod environments from one template
Version-controlled infrastructure with rollback capability on failure
services.tip: CloudFormation = IaC. CDK = define IaC in Python/TypeScript (generates CF). Terraform = third-party IaC.

services.name: AWS Well-Architected Tool
services.desc: Review your architectures against the 6 pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework and get improvement recommendations.
uses: Get a prioritized improvement plan for your workload's security posture
Benchmark architecture against best practices before a major launch
services.tip: 6 Pillars: Operational Excellence, Security, Reliability, Performance Efficiency, Cost Optimization, Sustainability.

services.name: AWS Service Catalog
services.desc: Create and manage catalogs of pre-approved IT products that teams can self-service — enforces standards and governance.
uses: Allow developers to deploy only approved CloudFormation templates
Standardize EC2 configurations and enforce tagging policies via catalog

services.name: Amazon Athena
services.desc: Serverless SQL query engine for data in S3. No infrastructure to manage — pay only for queries run. Uses Presto under the hood.
uses: Run ad hoc SQL on S3 access logs without loading them into a database
Analyze CloudTrail JSON logs with standard SQL queries instantly
services.tip: Athena = serverless SQL on S3. Pair with AWS Glue Data Catalog. No server setup — just query and pay per TB scanned.

services.name: AWS Glue
services.desc: Serverless ETL service + data catalog. Discover, prepare, and transform data for analytics. Glue Studio adds a visual drag-and-drop interface.
uses: Transform raw JSON in S3 into Parquet for Redshift loading (ETL)
Crawl S3 data to automatically build a central schema catalog for Athena
services.tip: Glue = ETL. Glue Data Catalog = metadata store shared with Athena and Redshift Spectrum.

services.name: AWS Glue Studio
services.desc: Visual drag-and-drop interface for building, running, and monitoring Glue ETL jobs — no coding required.
uses: Business analysts building ETL pipelines without writing Python/Scala
Visually map source-to-target transformations for data warehouse loads

services.name: Amazon QuickSight
services.desc: Serverless BI service for building interactive dashboards. ML-powered insights (anomaly detection, forecasting) built in. Pay-per-session pricing.
uses: Build sales dashboards shared across the organization from Redshift data
Embed interactive charts in a customer-facing SaaS application
services.tip: QuickSight = BI/dashboards. Athena = query. Redshift = warehouse. These three often appear together in exam scenarios.

services.name: AWS Kinesis
services.desc: Real-time streaming data platform. Kinesis Data Streams = ingest; Kinesis Data Firehose = load to S3/Redshift; Kinesis Analytics = SQL on streams.
uses: Real-time clickstream analysis for personalization on an e-commerce site
Ingest log data from 10,000 servers and load to S3 via Firehose
services.tip: Kinesis = real-time streaming. SQS = queuing (not real-time analytics). Exam: Firehose = no custom code, Streams = custom consumers.

services.name: Amazon OpenSearch Service
services.desc: Managed Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for log analytics, full-text search, and security analytics. Includes Kibana/OpenSearch Dashboards.
uses: Full-text search across millions of product listings on an e-commerce site
SIEM — centralize and analyze security logs for threat hunting

services.name: AWS Data Pipeline
services.desc: Managed ETL orchestration service to move and transform data between AWS services and on-premises data sources on a schedule.
uses: Nightly export from DynamoDB to S3 for reporting
Weekly load from on-prem Oracle database to Redshift

services.name: AWS Data Exchange
services.desc: Marketplace to find, subscribe to, and use third-party data sets in AWS. Delivers data directly to S3.
uses: Subscribe to financial market data for quantitative trading models
Access healthcare datasets from data providers for ML research

services.name: AWS Lake Formation
services.desc: Build, secure, and manage data lakes. Fine-grained access control at the table/column/row level across S3-based data lakes.
uses: Centralized governance — grant column-level access to sensitive data lake columns
Set up a certified data lake with security and audit trail in hours

services.name: AWS SageMaker
services.desc: End-to-end ML platform: build, train, tune, deploy, and monitor ML models at scale. Fully managed, supports all major frameworks.
uses: Train a custom fraud detection model on transaction data
One-click deploy a trained model as a real-time REST API endpoint
services.tip: SageMaker = the ML platform. Other AI services (Rekognition, Comprehend, etc.) are pre-trained — you use them via API.

services.name: Amazon Lex
services.desc: Build conversational chatbots with voice and text using the same technology that powers Alexa.
uses: Customer service chatbot handling FAQs and routing escalations
Voice-based IVR system for order tracking in a call center
services.tip: Lex = chatbot. Polly = text-to-speech. Transcribe = speech-to-text. Know which does what.

services.name: Amazon Transcribe
services.desc: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) — converts audio or video speech to text. Supports speaker diarization and custom vocabulary.
uses: Transcribe customer service call recordings for quality analysis
Auto-generate subtitles and closed captions for video content

services.name: Amazon Comprehend
services.desc: NLP service to find insights in text: sentiment, entities, key phrases, language detection, and custom classification.
uses: Sentiment analysis of thousands of product reviews automatically
Extract company names and locations from legal documents at scale

services.name: Amazon Textract
services.desc: ML service to extract text, forms, tables, and key-value pairs from scanned documents and images beyond simple OCR.
uses: Automate invoice processing by extracting line items and totals
Digitize mortgage applications by extracting form field data

services.name: Amazon Polly
services.desc: Convert text to lifelike speech using deep learning. Dozens of voices and languages. SSML support for controlling pronunciation.
uses: Add voice narration to an e-learning application
Accessibility features — read page content aloud for visually impaired users

services.name: Amazon Rekognition
services.desc: Image and video analysis: object detection, facial recognition, unsafe content detection, text in images, celebrity recognition.
uses: Facial recognition for employee building access control
Automatically detect and blur explicit content in user-uploaded images
services.tip: Rekognition = image/video AI. Textract = documents. Comprehend = text/NLP. Transcribe = audio.

services.name: Amazon Translate
services.desc: Neural machine translation for real-time and batch translation of text between 75+ languages.
uses: Translate product listings into 20 languages for a global marketplace
Real-time multilingual customer support chat translation

services.name: Amazon Forecast
services.desc: Fully managed time-series forecasting using ML. No ML experience needed — just provide historical data.
uses: Forecast product demand to optimize inventory levels
Predict server capacity needs for auto-scaling planning

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.desc: Managed generative AI service. Access foundation models (Claude, Llama, Titan, etc.) via API to build GenAI apps without managing infrastructure.
uses: Build a RAG-based knowledge assistant on internal documents
Text summarization and generation APIs for a content platform
services.tip: Bedrock = GenAI foundation models as a service. Key new exam topic for CLF-C02 GenAI domain.

services.name: AWS CodeCommit
services.desc: Managed private Git repositories in AWS. Fully integrated with other CodeSuite tools. Being deprecated — migrating to GitHub/GitLab.
uses: Host private Git repos for teams with IAM-based access control
Trigger CodePipeline on commits for CI/CD workflows

services.name: AWS CodeBuild
services.desc: Fully managed CI build service. Compile code, run tests, produce artifacts. No servers to manage. Pay per build minute.
uses: Run unit tests on every pull request and block merge on failure
Build Docker images and push to ECR as part of a CI pipeline
services.tip: CodeBuild = compile + test. CodeDeploy = deploy. CodePipeline = orchestrate all steps.

services.name: AWS CodeDeploy
services.desc: Automate application deployments to EC2, Lambda, ECS, and on-premises servers. Supports blue/green and rolling deployments.
uses: Zero-downtime blue/green deployments for a Node.js API on EC2
Automatic Lambda function version rollouts with traffic shifting
services.tip: CodeDeploy handles the actual DEPLOYMENT step. Different from CodeBuild (build) and CodePipeline (orchestration).

services.name: AWS CodePipeline
services.desc: Fully managed CI/CD pipeline. Orchestrates source → build → test → deploy stages using CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and third-party tools.
uses: Automate the full release workflow from Git push to production deploy
Multi-stage pipeline with manual approval gate before production release
services.tip: CodePipeline = the CI/CD ORCHESTRATOR. It chains CodeCommit + CodeBuild + CodeDeploy together.

services.name: AWS CodeStar
services.desc: Unified project management for setting up CI/CD toolchains quickly. Creates CodeCommit, CodeBuild, CodeDeploy, and CodePipeline in one click.
uses: Spin up a complete dev/deploy environment for a new project in minutes
Track all project activity, deployments, and issues in one dashboard

services.name: AWS Cloud9
services.desc: Cloud-based IDE accessible from any browser. Pre-configured for serverless development with built-in AWS CLI and Lambda debugger.
uses: Develop and debug Lambda functions without any local setup
Collaborative coding — share your IDE environment with a teammate

services.name: AWS X-Ray
services.desc: Distributed tracing service. Trace requests across microservices, visualize service maps, and identify performance bottlenecks.
uses: Identify which Lambda function call is causing 3-second latency in an API
Visualize service dependency map for a microservices architecture
services.tip: X-Ray = distributed tracing. CloudWatch = metrics/logs. Together they give full observability.

services.name: Amazon SQS
services.desc: Fully managed message queuing service. Decouples microservices, distributes tasks, and buffers asynchronous workloads. Standard and FIFO queues.
uses: Buffer order processing tasks to handle Black Friday traffic spikes
Decouple a web app from a slow order fulfillment service
services.tip: SQS = pull-based queue (consumers poll). SNS = push-based pub/sub. Often used together as SNS fan-out → multiple SQS queues.

services.name: Amazon SNS
services.desc: Fully managed pub/sub messaging and push notifications. One message published to a topic is delivered to all subscribers (Lambda, SQS, email, SMS, HTTP).
uses: Send SMS/email alerts to ops teams when CloudWatch alarm fires
Fan-out: one S3 event triggers parallel processing by multiple Lambda functions
services.tip: SNS topics → push to subscribers. SQS queues → consumers pull. Key exam pattern: SNS + SQS for fan-out.

services.name: Amazon MQ
services.desc: Managed message broker service for Apache ActiveMQ and RabbitMQ. Migrate existing message broker workloads to AWS with minimal code changes.
uses: Lift on-prem ActiveMQ broker to the cloud without rewriting app code
Hybrid cloud messaging between on-prem systems and AWS services
services.tip: MQ = for EXISTING apps using ActiveMQ/RabbitMQ protocols (AMQP, MQTT, STOMP). New apps should use SQS/SNS.

services.name: AWS EventBridge
services.desc: Serverless event bus. Route events from AWS services, SaaS apps, and custom apps to targets. Replaces CloudWatch Events.
uses: Route S3 events to multiple Lambda functions and Step Functions simultaneously
SaaS integration: Zendesk ticket events trigger Lambda workflows

services.name: AWS Step Functions
services.desc: Serverless visual workflow orchestration. Build state machines that coordinate Lambda, ECS, and other AWS services with retry logic, branching, and error handling.
uses: Orchestrate a 10-step order fulfillment workflow with retries on failures
Run ML data preparation pipeline with parallel processing steps
services.tip: Step Functions = complex multi-step workflows. Lambda = single function. Use Step Functions when you need orchestration.

services.name: AWS AppSync
services.desc: Managed GraphQL API service with real-time subscriptions and offline data sync. Connects to DynamoDB, Lambda, RDS, and HTTP sources.
uses: Build a real-time collaborative app where all users see live updates
Offline-capable mobile app that syncs data when connectivity is restored

services.name: AWS Amplify
services.desc: Full-stack platform to build, ship, and host web and mobile apps. CI/CD, hosting, auth (Cognito), storage (S3), and API (AppSync) in one toolkit.
uses: Deploy a Next.js app with CI/CD from GitHub in under 10 minutes
Add Cognito authentication and AppSync API to a React app without backend code

services.name: AWS Migration Hub
